title: Cheesy Chipotle Enchiladas
subtitle: with Rice and Avocado
description: Make your meat-free night Mexican with these enchiladas. Filled with rice, capsicum and a smoky tomato sauce, they’re a little bit spicy, a little bit saucy and deliciously cheesy.

steps.text: Cook rice: Preheat the oven to 220C. Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put in a small saucepan with 250ml (1 cup) water, cover and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 mins or until tender and the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and stand, covered, for at least 5 mins.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, cut the capsicum into 2cm chunks. Finely chop the avocado. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Coarsely grate the cheese. Lightly grease a 1.5L (6 cup) baking dish or ovenproof frypan (see Kitchen 101).

Make sauce: Put the chipotle (see Kitchen 101), tomatoes and 1 tsp sugar in a small saucepan over medium-high heat and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 mins or until thickened. Remove from the heat and season with salt and pepper.

Make rice filling: Meanwhile, heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Cook the capsicum and garlic, stirring, for 1 min. Add 1½ tbs tomato paste and 60ml (¼ cup) water. Bring to a simmer, then cook for 5 mins or until thickened. Stir in the rice and season with salt and pepper. Remove the pan from the heat.

Bake and serve up: Put the tortillas on a clean work surface and spread each with 1 tbs sauce. Spread the rice filling and half the cheese down the centre, roll to enclose, then put in the baking dish. Cover with the remaining sauce and scatter with the remaining cheese. Bake for 10-12 mins until golden and bubbling. Divide enchiladas among plates and scatter over the avocado.

Kitchen 101: You need a dish or ovenproof frypan large enough to fit the length of the tortillas – about 17cm x 26cm. Trim the ends of the tortillas, if needed, to fit the dish or pan. ~ Chipotle is a smoky Mexican condiment with a chilli kick, so reduce by half (or more) if there are kids around, or if you aren't a big chilli fan.
